title: Stability of Shifted Complexes via the Second-Moment Defect of the Up-Laplacian
summary: Let $K$ be a finite pure $k$-dimensional simplicial complex, with $k\ge1$, on the vertex set $[n]$ and with facet family $K_k$. Let $λ_1(K)\geλ_2(K)\ge\cdots>0$ be the nonzero eigenvalues of its $(k-1)$-dimensional up-Laplacian, and, after ordering the vertices so that $°_K(1)\ge\cdots\ge°_K(n)$, let $\dvT{r}(K)$ be the number of vertices contained in at least $r$ facets. A complex is \emph{shifted} if replacing a vertex of a face by a smaller vertex outside the face always yields another face.
